done_when: In a repo whose tests run in CI, forge merge after main moved pushes the merged branch and waits for the pull request checks instead of running tests on the laptop, and a repo whose tests run on the laptop keeps today's local retest

known.title: Wait for the CI configuration used to skip the local retest
Combined-head CI can omit tests added by main
Gate: existing merge regression tests fail under the new routing

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a CI-enabling pull request is combined after main moves, its check wait fails or times out, and merge is retried.
The first attempt saves the combined head before waiting (src/forge/merge.py:153–154). On retry, that head already contains main, so the retest block does not run and line 129 does not load the branch's configuration. The wait at line 159 instead uses the default-branch configuration loaded at line 48. If main still says `test_place = "local"`, Forge skips the wait entirely; if required check names changed, it waits for the old names. When branch protection has not yet been updated to require the new tests check, GitHub can accept the merge while that check is pending or failing. [GitHub branch rules](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets)
findings.title: Wait for the CI configuration used to skip the local retest

why: When tests run in CI and main moved before a merge, forge merge retests the merged branch on the laptop test lane for every repo except Python apps with broad pytest selection, so client merges wait in the laptop queue
